name: Direct z0/z1 policy-separation loss (ZSEP) -- 6th crossover-preservation attempt
authority: PI, 2026-09-04, queuing a candidate 6th attempt while the BCS sealed EVAL runs, in direct response to the z0/z1 behavior-characterization finding: opponent identity drives behavior 5-15x more than latent z does on the incumbent checkpoint
QUESTION: Does directly rewarding z0 and z1 for producing different action distributions on the same state -- rather than working around the symptom via retention, trunk-freezing, or supervision balance -- close the gap the behavior characterization found (z0-vs-z1 shifts of 0.02-0.08 vs opponent-driven shifts of 0.38-0.58)?

MECHANISM_ALREADY_EXISTS_CONFIRMED_BEFOR.what_it_does: per-agent, per-action-head pairwise Jensen-Shannon divergence between z0's and z1's action distributions on the SAME batch of states, hinged at a margin: loss = mean(relu(margin - JSD)). Zero cost once JSD clears the margin; nonzero gradient pressure pushing the two policies apart while it doesn't.
MECHANISM_ALREADY_EXISTS_CONFIRMED_BEFOR.confirmed_zero_in_every_prior_run_this_p: every preset in the v5_repertoire/v3i_consequence lineage (what V4.build_config() and therefore every one of CCP-S2/RSCFT/trunk-freeze/SAC-RFT/BCS descends from) explicitly sets this to 0.0. An EARLIER, unrelated preset family (v3i_specialization.py, a different architecture generation) used nonzero values (0.015-0.20) -- not evidence this program's architecture was ever tested with it on, only that the mechanism itself is implemented and was exercised somewhere in this codebase's history.
MECHANISM_ALREADY_EXISTS_CONFIRMED_BEFOR.gating_confirmed_open_for_our_recipe: SeparationObjective.compute() requires counterfactual_active=True and NOT hparams.fixed_latent_strategy. Traced rl/custom_ppo/update/phase_policy.py:resolve_training_phase() -> our production recipe (V4.build_config(), no v6i1_curriculum) resolves phase='__legacy__', whose PhaseTrainingPolicy has counterfactual_active=True by the fallback branch. fixed_latent_strategy is False during training (z sampled per episode, confirmed by every prior run's 'Summer-plan audit' banner). No additional wiring is needed beyond setting the coefficient -- confirmed by reading the gating code path, not assumed.

margin_and_gate_params_left_at_config_de.why_defaults_not_tuned: changing these alongside the coefficient would be a second and third changed variable. Left at whatever this codebase already ships as its own baseline so ONLY the coefficient is new.

HONEST_TRADEOFF_DISCLOSED_BEFORE_THE_RUN.this_differs_in_kind_from_attempts_1_thr: CCP-S2/RSCFT/trunk-freeze/SAC-RFT/BCS all left the base PPO+latent training objective unchanged and added or modified an AUXILIARY mechanism (causal supervision, retention, parameter freezing, sampling balance) around it. This experiment changes the base objective itself -- it directly rewards divergence rather than removing an obstacle to naturally-emerging divergence.
HONEST_TRADEOFF_DISCLOSED_BEFORE_THE_RUN.risk: a hinge JSD loss can be satisfied by ANY sufficiently different action distribution, not specifically one that makes z0 the better choice against Pole A and z1 the better choice against Pole B. It is possible for this loss to produce measurably separated but tactically arbitrary or even counterproductive divergence -- 'different for the sake of being different' rather than 'different because each is the right counter to its pole.' The PRIMARY_GATE below is what actually distinguishes those two outcomes; passing the gate, not merely moving JSD, is the bar.
HONEST_TRADEOFF_DISCLOSED_BEFORE_THE_RUN.not_omitted_or_downplayed: this caveat is recorded here, before any training step, specifically so a PASS cannot be reported without this context and a FAIL cannot be read as surprising.

THE_ONE_CHANGED_VARIABLE.changed: latent_actor_z_separation_coef: 0.0 (every prior arm) REPLACED BY 0.02 for TREATMENT (CONTROL stays at 0.0)
unchanged: full network trainable, no trunk freeze

no causal supervision loss in EITHER arm (this experiment isolates the separation loss alone, not stacked on top of CCP-S2's causal bank -- matches the CONTROL convention CCP-S2/trunk-freeze already established: a no-causal-loss arm as the clean baseline)
no retention mechanism of any kind
separation margin and gate parameters (left at PPOConfig defaults, see above)

DISCLOSED_HORIZON_DEVIATION.prior_standard: every arm in CCP-S2/RSCFT/trunk-freeze/SAC-RFT/BCS used 500,000 additional steps (matched horizon for comparability against each other)
DISCLOSED_HORIZON_DEVIATION.this_experiment: 250,000 additional steps for BOTH arms (still matched to each other within this experiment)
DISCLOSED_HORIZON_DEVIATION.why: this loss applies gradient pressure on every PPO minibatch, unlike the causal-bank-based mechanisms which fire only every cadence=4 minibatches against a 772-row (5-segment) bank -- a much denser training signal per step, so less wall-clock exposure is plausibly needed to see whether it moves the gate at all. Also a direct response to deadline pressure (Sept 15) with 4v4/6v6 still required regardless of this outcome.
DISCLOSED_HORIZON_DEVIATION.consequence: a FAIL at 250k steps is weaker evidence against this mechanism than a FAIL at 500k would be (the effect could still be building). This is disclosed as a limitation of this specific test, not elided. If the PI wants a matched-horizon confirmation later, that is a separate decision, not implied by this run.

MECHANICAL_PREFLIGHT_REQUIRED_BEFORE_ANY: policy_z_separation_loss produces a nonzero, finite loss and nonzero actor gradients on a real batch from the real incumbent checkpoint

--verify-steps wiring check under REAL training (same pattern as every prior stage) confirming actor parameters move and, for TREATMENT specifically, that pairwise JSD (the diagnostic already printed every update, sep_JSD/max_JSD) trends upward relative to CONTROL over the verification window

PRIMARY_GATE.criterion: delta_A > 0 AND LCB95(delta_A) > 0 AND delta_B > 0 AND LCB95(delta_B) > 0
PRIMARY_GATE.rule: same primary gate as every prior stage. No mercy, no reinterpretation.

ATTRIBUTION.statistic: preregistered PAIRED bootstrap over the shared 64 seeds, n_boot=20000, alpha=0.05, rng_seed=7

EVAL_PROTOCOL.SECONDARY_DIAGNOSTIC_NOT_A_GATE: mean pairwise JSD between z0 and z1 on the EVAL rollouts themselves (not just training-time diagnostics) -- reported regardless of PRIMARY_GATE outcome, to distinguish 'separation loss increased JSD but didn't help win rate' from 'separation loss did nothing measurable at all'

PREREGISTERED_INTERPRETATION.reading: direct separation pressure recovered crossover where nothing else did -- the strongest positive result this whole program could produce
crossover recovered under both; separation loss not necessary under this run

direct separation pressure also insufficient at this horizon/coefficient -- either the mechanism needs more steps/a larger coefficient than tested here, or the erosion driver is not (only) collapsed z-conditioning

EVAL_PROTOCOL.tie_or_reversal: any tie or reversal triggers a row-level integrity audit before interpretation, written before its rows are read -- same standard as every prior stage

PROGRAM_TERMINATION_RULE.status_relative_to_the_ladder: this is a CANDIDATE attempt, queued behind BCS's sealed EVAL result and the calendar -- not yet authorized to consume GPU time. Building the spec and mechanism now (while BCS's EVAL runs) does not itself authorize the production runs; that is a separate, explicit go/no-go once BCS resolves.
PROGRAM_TERMINATION_RULE.if_this_also_fails: six independent, principled mechanisms (retention x2, trunk-freeze, supervision balance, direct separation) failing the same gate is a strong, publishable negative result in its own right -- not a reason to keep inventing a seventh without a fresh, equally concrete piece of evidence the way this one had (the behavior characterization) and BCS had (the pre-logged 3.5x supervision imbalance).
